title: Epigastric Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. Exam reveals epigastric tenderness with guarding, jaundiced sclera, and possibly Grey Turner/Cullen signs in severe cases. Most common causes: gallstones (GET SMASHED mnemonic — Gallstones, Ethanol, Trauma, Steroids, Mumps, Autoimmune, Scorpion stings, Hypercalcemia/Hypertriglyceridemia, ERCP, Drugs). Diagnosis requires 2 of 3: (1) characteristic epigastric pain, (2) lipase/amylase >3x upper limit, (3) CT findings. Lipase is more sensitive and specific than amylase (especially in delayed presentation). Ranson criteria and BISAP score for severity. Management: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (LR preferred over NS), NPO initially, IV analgesics (morphine OK), antiemetics. Early enteral nutrition within 24-48h (NG or NJ feeds). ERCP within 24h if gallstone pancreatitis with cholangitis or obstruction. CT with contrast at 48-72h if not improving to assess for necrosis/complications.
chief_complaint: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back, nausea, vomiting

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Assess severity — may appear very ill.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Epigastric tenderness + guarding. Grey Turner (flank) / Cullen (periumbilical) in severe hemorrhagic pancreatitis.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP / LFTs
stacks.finding: Elevated AST/ALT/ALP/bilirubin if gallstone etiology. Elevated BUN ≥20 at 48h = poor prognosis.

stacks.label: Lipase
stacks.finding: >3x ULN = diagnostic. More sensitive and specific than amylase.

stacks.label: RUQ ultrasound
stacks.finding: Check for gallstones — most common cause.

stacks.label: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
stacks.finding: At 48-72h if not improving. Assess for necrosis, pseudocyst, abscess.

stacks.label: IV fluids (Lactated Ringer preferred)
stacks.finding: Aggressive resuscitation. LR preferred over NS — reduces systemic inflammation. 250-500 mL/hr initially.

stacks.label: Diet, NPO
stacks.finding: Initially NPO for bowel rest. Advance to clear liquids as pain improves.

stacks.label: IV analgesics (Morphine / Hydromorphone)
stacks.finding: Pain management. Morphine is acceptable — does NOT worsen pancreatitis (old teaching was incorrect).

physical_exam.respiratory: May have decreased breath sounds (pleural effusion).
physical_exam.abdominal: Epigastric tenderness with guarding. Assess for Grey Turner (flank ecchymosis) and Cullen (periumbilical ecchymosis) — retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

decoys.label: Prophylactic antibiotics in all pancreatitis
decoys.reason_wrong: Antibiotics NOT indicated for sterile pancreatic necrosis. Only for confirmed infected necrosis or concurrent infection. Prophylaxis does not improve outcomes.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: (1) Epigastric pain, (2) Lipase >3x ULN, (3) CT findings. Lipase > amylase (more sensitive/specific). Ranson/BISAP for severity scoring.
LR preferred over NS. 250-500 mL/hr. NPO initially. Early enteral feeds within 24-48h reduce infectious complications. ERCP within 24h if gallstone + cholangitis.

case_summary: Acute pancreatitis (likely gallstone). Epigastric pain radiating to back + jaundice + lipase >3x ULN. Aggressive LR IV fluids + NPO + pain control. RUQ US → CT at 48-72h if not improving.
